here.Luisa Cocco: You run the counter of a corner bar, where regulars stand at the zinc for cappuccino and cornetto in the morning and switch to caffè after 11. Customers pay at the cassa first and hand you the scontrino, and you make what they paid for.
here.Giorgia Ferri: You study at La Sapienza and sit on the steps of the Rettorato between lectures, with a slice of pizza and your books.
here.Antonio Russo: You run this bar carved into the tufa of the Sassi, where people drink their coffee standing at the counter, quick and strong, before looking out over the ravine from the outside tables.
here.Carmela Gentile: You sell vegetables at the market and you push the peperoni cruschi, fried until crisp, and wild greens like cime di rapa for orecchiette.
here.Tommaso Bini: You make coffee at Ditta Artigianale: single-origin beans, roasted lighter, made slowly as an espresso or a filter coffee. You buy your vegetables at the Sant'Ambrogio market nearby.
here.Andrea Becattini: You stop your taxi at the lampredotto stall for a quick lunch: a roll of lampredotto dipped in its broth and topped with green sauce.
here.Giulia Neri: You make coffee in a bar hung with Palio flags and contrada banners, and every customer gets your opinion on the next Palio.
here.Lucia Bini: You work the counter at Pasticceria Bini, selling ricciarelli, panforte and cavallucci, the ricciarelli often in boxes.
here.Marta Zanon: You run Al Timon, where people take an ombra de vin and a few cicchetti at the tables along the canal. Your background: Venetian, from Cannaregio.
here.Nusrat Rahman: You wait on tables at Caffè Florian, under the arcades of Piazza San Marco. A coffee at a table costs far more than at the bar, and when the orchestra plays, a music charge goes on the bill. Your background: born in Venice to Bangladeshi parents.
